summary: Created OpenRC-managed service "inventory-worker" on node1 that runs a long-running shell loop confined via bubblewrap: root filesystem read-only, /var/lib/inventory the only writable bind mount, running as unprivileged uid 1001 (dedicated "inventory" user), with NoNewPrivs=1 enforced (bwrap default, verified). Service enabled in the default runlevel. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id/boot time/service+data health, issued a native reboot whose ack returned before disconnection, polled through the outage, confirmed a new boot_id/boot time post-restart, and verified the service auto-started and resumed writing inventory snapshots.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Alpine 3.23, OpenRC, root shell) to determine init system and available sandboxing tools
Installed bubblewrap (bwrap) via apk from the community repo
Created dedicated unprivileged user 'inventory' (uid 1001) with home/data dir /var/lib/inventory (0750, owned by inventory:inventory)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh: a loop that writes a periodic snapshot + log line into /var/lib/inventory every 10s
Validated bwrap confinement manually: root read-only (touch /etc and /root denied), /var/lib/inventory writable, NoNewPrivs=1 confirmed via /proc/self/status
Created /etc/init.d/inventory-worker OpenRC service running bwrap as command_user inventory:inventory, backgrounded, with stdout/stderr logs inside /var/lib/inventory
Started the service, verified running state, process uid/gid 1001, NoNewPrivs=1 on the live pid, and growing snapshot/log files
Enabled inventory-worker in the OpenRC 'default' runlevel for boot persistence
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, boot time, service status, latest snapshot/log content
Issued a backgrounded delayed 'reboot' so the acknowledgement returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified new boot_id and later boot time (proof of actual restart, not just service restart)
Verified post-restart: service auto-started via runlevel, running under uid 1001 confined via bwrap, and actively writing new incrementing snapshots/log entries

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker deployed as a managed OpenRC service, long-running
evidence.summary: Created /etc/init.d/inventory-worker; rc-service start succeeded; process confirmed alive and producing incrementing snapshots over time
Inside the bwrap sandbox: touch /root/should-fail -> Permission denied, touch /etc/should-fail -> Read-only file system, touch /var/lib/inventory/ok-write succeeded
NoNewPrivs:1 verified both directly inside the sandboxed shell and via /proc/<pid>/status of the live running service process

evidence.requirement: Service runs unprivileged, not as root
evidence.summary: Dedicated inventory user uid/gid 1001 created; live service process Uid/Gid confirmed as 1001 via /proc/<pid>/status
rc-update add inventory-worker default succeeded; post-restart rc-update show default lists inventory-worker, confirming it actually started on boot
Captured boot_id b8b79528-..., boot time 2026-09-04 23:05:18, rc-service status 'started', and current inventory snapshot/log content
Backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' returned REBOOT_SCHEDULED immediately; subsequent call confirmed connection reset, proving reboot executed after ack

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart (node1)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from b8b79528-995d-4a3b-ac14-3a3b0d4e81c8 to 6c4c8894-a050-4fed-864d-bb6228626607; boot time advanced from 23:05:18 to 23:07:46

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service and data (node1)
evidence.summary: After restart: rc-service status 'started', inventory-worker present in default runlevel, bwrap-confined process running as uid 1001, and inventory-snapshot.txt/worker.log showing a fresh sequence starting again and incrementing
